slots.title: US session recap — Aug. 27, 2026
slots.body:
US equity indexes finished the 2026-08-27 cash session with small losses.
The S&P 500 closed at 7,675.70, essentially flat at 0.0%.
The Nasdaq Composite was 26,130.20, down 0.1%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.2% to 53,463.88, and the Russell 2000 was 3,005.90, down 0.1%.

Volatility eased: the VIX settled at 15.21, down 1.6% from 15.45, with an intraday band of 15.21 to 15.74.

On Nasdaq sector averages, Real Estate led at +1.2%, followed by Energy at +1.0% and Technology at +0.9%.
Communication Services lagged at -1.7%, with Consumer Defensive and Consumer Cyclical both around -0.6%.

Megacap technology saw mixed closes.
NVIDIA finished at 209.66, down 1.6%, on heavy volume in the actives list.
Meta Platforms rose 1.1% to 576.14.
Amazon was off 0.3% at 260.28, and AMD was up 0.4% at 480.93.

Oracle closed up 2.8% at 148.84; Marvell gained 2.0% to 245.11; Autodesk added 1.4% to 254.77; Workday fell 1.9% to 190.75 — all names on the Aug. 27 earnings calendar in the injected data.

Eli Lilly was a notable drag among large caps, down 3.5% to 1,190.03.
Johnson & Johnson lost 1.1% to 270.00.
UnitedHealth rose 1.1% to 401.01.
Tesla closed at 345.82, down 1.3%.

Retail and consumer names on the same calendar showed varied reactions: Gap finished up 5.0% at 21.15; Best Buy gained 2.5% to 87.44; Ulta rose 1.1% to 543.19; Dollar Tree fell 1.7% to 132.18; Dollar General was roughly flat, up 0.2% at 122.79.

Energy equities diverged from the sector average: Exxon Mobil fell 1.5% to 158.20 while Chevron ticked up 0.2% to 200.25.
Brent crude in the cross-asset set was 85.54, down 1.3%; the United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 1.0% at 127.35.

Gold futures (GCUSD) closed at 4,658.40, up 0.1%.
The dollar proxy UUP rose 0.3% to 28.02.
Bitcoin was 78,802.51, down 0.3%.
EUR/USD was unchanged at 1.17 in the injected quote.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-08-25 in the data showed a 10-year yield of 4.6% and a 2s10s spread of 0.47 percentage points.

The economic calendar listed high-impact US releases at 12:30 ET on Aug. 27 for initial jobless claims, continuing claims, the four-week average, and the goods trade balance; the injected bundle did not include released actuals for those prints.

Overseas indexes in the file were modestly softer: Nikkei 225 -0.2%, FTSE 100 -0.3%, Hang Seng -0.4%.

Among liquid movers in the screen, Abercrombie & Fitch led gainers at +35.7% to 147.75; several low-priced actives showed extreme percentage moves, separate from the large-cap core of the session.
